questions.q: What does the summary name as a common root of harsh self-criticism?
a: Having a parent who was very critical in childhood
Being praised constantly as a young child
Growing up with too many siblings
Starting a demanding career as an adult
questions.why: Lesson 1 links self-criticism to critical parenting in childhood.

questions.q: Why might a child start criticizing themselves before a parent can?
a: To avoid hearing the criticism from the parent
To earn rewards for good behavior
To compete with brothers and sisters
To copy what teachers do at school
questions.why: Lesson 1 says children criticize themselves to preempt a parent's criticism.

questions.q: What exercise does the summary offer for beginning self-compassion?
a: Treat yourself as you would a friend who is hurting
List the achievements you are proudest of
Compare your progress with people you admire
Repeat compliments about yourself each morning
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests imagining what you would do for a friend facing the same struggle.

questions.q: What does the story of a friend falling on ice illustrate?
a: We comfort a friend but scold ourselves for the same slip
We hide our pain from the people closest to us
We judge strangers more kindly than friends
We recover faster when nobody is watching
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts our harsh self-talk with the care we give a friend.

questions.q: Which two practices does the summary say make you good at self-care?
a: Mindfulness and putting distance between you and your pain
Willpower and repeating positive affirmations
Planning and strict time management
Exercise and a strong social network
questions.why: Lesson 3 combines mindfulness with psychological distance from pain.
